name: Heterophyes heterophyes

taxonomy.rank_note: Reference groups can include multiple species. Protozoan higher-rank systems differ; the lineage is provided without forcing every clade into a class rank.

morphology: Egg: about 28–30 × 15–17 µm; small brown operculated egg containing a miracidium.
Adult reproductive structures support taxonomic identification when recovered.

transmission.detail: Snail stages infect fish; ingested fish metacercariae become intestinal adults.

life_cycle.detail: Snail stages infect fish; ingested fish metacercariae become intestinal adults.

hosts: Definitive: humans, cats, dogs and other fish-eating animals. Intermediate: snail then freshwater or brackish-water fish.
distribution: Foci in the Middle East and parts of Asia; confirm the actual exposure region instead of assuming Thai endemicity.
clinical_significance: Abdominal pain and diarrhea; rare extraintestinal complications have been linked to egg migration.
diagnostics: Concentrated stool wet mounts at 400×; species confirmation may need adults or molecular methods.
differential_diagnosis: Eggs are difficult to separate from Metagonimus and other small operculated flukes.
review_status: Source-compiled educational content; not independently clinically validated
description: Heterophyes heterophyes — Heterophyid intestinal fluke. Abdominal pain and diarrhea; rare extraintestinal complications have been linked to egg migration.

annotation_guidance: Record specimen, stage, stain, objective/total magnification, pixel calibration, source image and reviewer certainty.
Native crops of 200–650 pixels do not determine biological size. Retain µm-per-pixel calibration before resizing.
Split training, validation and test data by patient/specimen; keep related crops in the same split.
Keep damaged or ambiguous objects uncertain. Molecular confirmation of a mixed specimen does not assign every pictured object a species.
